nodes.title: SG-3 Add lighting and atmosphere effects
nodes.body:
Context: buildEffects (game/src/engine/buildEffects.ts) and createPhaserEffectContext (game/frontend/src/phaser/effectContext.ts) already support dust, ambientLight and transition effects. The bedroom scene declares only those. Desired behaviour: the bedroom also shows a moonlight shaft, lamp glow, light under the door and a soft vignette, all declared in content, drawn on the effects layer with palette colours, with dust using the generated effect:dust sprite, and every Phaser object destroyed on scene shutdown. Why: section 3.4 of the goal requires layered 2D lighting and particles.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the bedroom scene content, when buildEffects runs with a mocked context, then createEffect is called once for each of dust, ambientLight, moonlightShaft, lampGlow, doorLight and vignette, with depth equal to layerDepth('effects')
- Given any created effect, when the scene shuts down, then destroy is called on every handle
- Given the bedroom scene content, when its effect colours are read, then each colour is a member of PALETTE


## Scope
- In scope: effect schema types
- In scope: bedroom effects content
- In scope: Phaser effect context
- In scope: destroy helper
- Out of scope: new rooms
- Out of scope: new story content
- Out of scope: backend changes
- Out of scope: audio
- Out of scope: deployment
- Out of scope: repository clean-up
- Preserve: Phaser 3.90.x pin
- Preserve: existing dust, ambientLight and transition behaviour
- Preserve: data-driven scene content
- Preserve: 480x270 resolution


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x
- Scene content stays data-driven: no effect position or asset id hardcoded in a scene class
- One shared palette of at most 48 colours
- Tests are unit tests with all dependencies mocked


## Definition of done
- All requirements delivered with Act and Verify units green


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Scene content declares moonlight shaft, lamp glow, door light and vignette with palette colours
nodes.body:

Desired: add moonlightShaft, lampGlow, doorLight and vignette variants and author them in bedroom.yaml with palette hex colours. nodes.title: REQ · Phaser effect context renders each lighting effect on the effects layer and destroys it
nodes.body:
Context: effectContext.ts switch handles dust, ambientLight and transition. Desired: render moonlightShaft, lampGlow, doorLight and vignette as Phaser game objects at spec.depth, with a destroy that removes every object it created. Dust keeps using resolveKey(spec.asset), the generated dust sprite.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given each new effect spec, when createEffect runs with a mocked scene, then a game object is added with setDepth(spec.depth)
- Given a vignette handle, when destroy runs, then every band object it created is destroyed
- Given a dust spec, when createEffect runs, then particles use the key returned by resolveKey for effect:dust


## Scope
- In scope: game/frontend/src/phaser/effectContext.ts
- Out of scope: content changes
- Preserve: existing dust and ambientLight rendering


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x
- Use only Phaser 3.90 APIs


## Dependencies
- REQ1


## Definition of done
- All effect types rendered and destroyable


## Non-functional requirements
- Colours parsed from spec hex, no literals


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · buildEffects places all effects on the effects layer and a helper destroys them on shutdown
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene SHUTDOWN handler loops handles with forEach. Desired: export destroyEffects(handles) from buildEffects.ts that destroys every handle and tolerates a throwing handle so the others are still destroyed; BootScene calls it. Why: Phaser effects created from content must be destroyed on shutdown.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given handles where one destroy throws, when destroyEffects runs, then every other handle's destroy is still called
- Given a scene with six non-transition effects, when buildEffects runs, then each createEffect call carries depth layerDepth('effects')
- Given BootScene shutdown, when it fires, then destroyEffects is called with the created handles


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/engine/buildEffects.ts
- In scope: game/frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts shutdown handler
- Out of scope: new effect types
- Preserve: buildEffects skipping transition specs


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x


## Dependencies
- REQ1


## Definition of done
- BootScene uses destroyEffects


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.body:
Implement the new cases with Phaser 3.90 game objects at spec.depth and destroy handles removing all created objects.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each new case sets depth to spec.depth
- Vignette destroy removes all bands


## Scope

- Colour comes from spec

## Dependencies

- None
nodes.description: Implement the new cases with Phaser 3.90 game objects at spec.depth and destroy handles removing all created objects.
acceptance_criteria: Each new case sets depth to spec.depth
Vignette destroy removes all bands

steps.action: Add a module-level helper parseColor(hex: string): number returning parseInt(hex.slice(1), 16), and use it in the ambientLight case too.
steps.expected: ambientLight still passes the same numeric colour

steps.action: Add case 'moonlightShaft' and case 'doorLight': each adds scene.add.rectangle(area.x, area.y, area.width, area.height, parseColor(spec.color), spec.alpha).setOrigin(0).setDepth(spec.depth).setBlendMode('ADD') and returns { destroy: () => rect.destroy() }.
steps.expected: Each case returns a handle whose destroy destroys one rectangle

steps.action: Add case 'lampGlow': scene.add.circle(spec.x, spec.y, spec.radius, parseColor(spec.color), spec.alpha).setDepth(spec.depth).setBlendMode('ADD'); destroy destroys the circle.
steps.expected: A circle is added at depth spec.depth

steps.action: Add case 'vignette': for each lineWidth in [24, 16, 8] create scene.add.rectangle(w/2, h/2, w, h) with w=scene.scale.width, h=scene.scale.height, then .setStrokeStyle(lineWidth, parseColor(spec.color), spec.alpha / 3).setDepth(spec.depth); collect in an array; destroy destroys all.
steps.code:
const bands = [24, 16, 8].map((lw) => scene.add.rectangle(w / 2, h / 2, w, h).setStrokeStyle(lw, parseColor(spec.color), spec.alpha / 3).setDepth(spec.depth));
return { destroy: () => bands.forEach((b) => b.destroy()) };
steps.expected: Three bands created and all destroyed together
